title: How to Do a Wall Push-Up for Beginners
intro: The wall push-up is the easiest push-up version and can be done at home or in the office pantry. It's great for starting to build upper body strength without pressure on your knees and wrists.
muscles: Chest, front shoulders, back of the arms (triceps) and core. Honest note: this exercise strengthens your arms, but it doesn't specifically remove arm fat. Fat goes down from your whole body through eating and daily movement.
steps: Stand facing a wall, about one arm's length away.
Place your palms on the wall at shoulder height, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Tighten your tummy, body straight from head to heels.
Bend your elbows and slowly bring your chest towards the wall.
Push the wall to return to the starting position while breathing out.
mistakes: Standing too close to the wall. The movement becomes too short and less effective.
Arching your lower back or sticking your bum out. Keep your body straight like a plank of wood.
Moving your head first. Your chest should move towards the wall, neck stays neutral.
easier: Stand closer to the wall and do a smaller movement.
harder: Move your feet further from the wall. Once it's easy, switch to a kitchen counter or sturdy table, then knee push-ups.
dose: 2-3 sets x 10-15 reps, 3 times a week. You can also do 1 set during your office break.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your shoulders, elbows or wrists. If you have just given birth or have a shoulder injury, get clearance from a doctor or physio first.

faq.q: Do wall push-ups actually work? They look so easy.
faq.a: Yes, especially for beginners. The key is clean technique and making it slightly harder bit by bit by moving your feet further from the wall.

faq.q: Can I do them every day?
faq.a: Yes, since the load is light. But if your muscles are still sore, rest a day. 3 times a week is enough to build strength.

faq.q: Is it suitable for mums who just gave birth?
faq.a: Wall push-ups are usually one of the gentler options, but everyone is different. Get your doctor's clearance first, especially after surgery or if you have separated abs.
